The Helan Mountains, sometimes called a "mountain island in the sky," separate the semi-arid Ordos Plateau and the Yellow River Valley from the arid deserts of the Alxa Plateau to the west. Like the rugged ranges of western North America's Great Basin, the Helan Range holds dense conifer forests and may support plant and animal communities found nowhere else. We are working to reduce operational costs by developing an ultra-high efficiency InGaN solar cell. As shown in Fig. 15, the alitrunk is conspicuously swollen and sits much higher than the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum bears a pair of strong spines that are straight to slightly upcurved. There is no metanotal groove, and the metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous. In profile the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes down posteriorly, giving a short posterior face. On the postpetiole the anterior and dorsal surfaces form a single convexity, and the posterior face is truncated. In dorsal view the nodes of both petiole and postpetiole are broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. These rugae are irregular and meander slightly, and a few anastomoses are usually present. The scrobal area is mostly smooth, though it usually carries 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and this sculpture runs around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between the rugae are unsculptured, or at most show faint superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose, while the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. All dorsal surfaces of the head and body are densely clothed with fine, acute hairs. The color ranges from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 contains the coding sequence for prhI from *Ralstonia solanacearum*. PrhI is an ECF sigma factor required for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. PrhR activates the gene, which then directs sigma factor expression through activation of the PprhJ promoter. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 contains the PprhJ promoter region. The promoter responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and PrhI activates it. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here is a summary of what we found regarding foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a expression was highly restricted in the male, while the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

foxl2b expression in adult female tissues was also restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, foxl2b expression was very strong, which agrees with earlier findings showing foxl2b present alongside the absence of foxl2a in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Taken together, these results suggest that foxl2b may act as a critical regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Thank you for your interest in our research.

However, Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot support carbon neutrality claims for electrical use beyond a claimant's metered consumption, since most RECs come from projects that would have been financially viable without their sale. [10] Consequently, they lack the essential attribute of additionality. Additionality looks at the counterfactual: what would have happened under the status quo had the REC not been purchased or contracted. Although there are many frameworks for testing additionality, the core question stays the same: did the project's financial survival depend on REC revenues? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation following the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975), and from it obtained a higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows that the modified curvature terms of the MMSE matter, while the slope square terms remain negligible, as the mild-slope assumption requires. We therefore kept all the modified curvature terms that the MSE neglects, and this gave us a uniform model.

We then built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering over a varying bottom. In general, the uniform model reproduces the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, the uniform model agrees more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than the results of Kirby (1986).

The FEM model can also be applied to wave transformation over arbitrarily varying bathymetry.

The myth of the Phaedrus is more intense than anything that came before it, though it belongs to a different order of ideas. It speaks of a former existence rather than a future one, and it describes a deep conflict between reason, strengthened by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts within us. In that earlier life, the human soul accompanied some god and beheld truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present existence is the outcome of a struggle that took place before it. This world is a relative construct, often projected into a future, in the same way that we wonder where men were before their birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it carries as much force and reaches as widely as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech, and the majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," can only be rendered inadequately in another language.

Subject: A Note on Buraq

Dear Friend,

For most of history, people saw the world as a blend of reality and myth, and only modern comparative biology drew a clear line between the two. Science has not removed the space in between, though, and that is where a figure like Buraq lives. Such transitional figures help us hold together empirical knowledge and spiritual experience, which can otherwise seem unrelated.

Buraq still appears in contemporary culture as a bridge between rational classification and the older power of myth. Nowhere is this clearer than in the Islamic transport industry, where she recurs as a kind of patron saint, combining piety and speed. Airlines from Libya to Indonesia carry her name, as do bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and Pakistan's first drone.

Part of the reason Buraq adapts so easily to commerce is that she functions as both an aesthetic and a linguistic object. She presides over wings and wheels, but her name is also used to sell plastic and PVC, heavy metal, heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

When King's Cross station expanded north in the mid-1860s, its tracks cut through the churchyard of St. Pancras Old Church, the oldest Christian site of worship in London. Thomas Hardy, who was working as an architect at the time, was given the job of clearing the land. He exhumed the dead and arranged their gravestones in a spiral around a central tree. The tree still stands, but its roots have grown around the stones, and the inscriptions are becoming harder to read.

Elsewhere in the cemetery, monuments mark the graves of other notable figures. Mary Wollstonecraft, author of *A Vindication of the Rights of Woman* (1792) and mother of Mary Shelley, who wrote *Frankenstein* (1818), is buried there. Nearby stands an imposing mausoleum bearing the name Sir John Soane, the collector-architect whose eccentric house remains on Lincoln's Inn Fields, as documented in the *Description of the House and Museum of Sir John Soane* (1835).

Welcome to MapleStory. There are thousands of monsters roaming the world, but here is a quick breakdown of where they live and how to survive.

The weak monsters are the most common foes, and you will find them by towns. They wander aimlessly, even if you bump into them, so just take the damage that comes from them.

The dangerous ones live deep in dungeons.

The aggro mechanic matters. Monsters normally roam aimlessly, even if you bump into them. But if you attack or cast a debuff on an enemy, you aggro it. That means you get its attention, and it will try to attack you back.

The behavioral pattern of most enemies is to attack by trying to run into you over and over again. Against these persistent attackers, the best strategy is simply to attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place. Sometimes you will need to jump over them, which is a good dodge tactic to avoid their attacks entirely.

For the full details, check out the complete list at MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

This ecoregion covers the moist deciduous forests that surround the montane rainforests in the northern part of the Western Ghats, in Maharashtra and Karnataka in western India. The region's origins go back to Gondwana. During the Cretaceous period, the Deccan Plate broke away from Gondwanaland, drifted north, and eventually rejoined the northern Eurasian continent. Later geological uplift formed the Western Ghats Mountains, which caught the southwestern monsoon rains and created a moisture gradient: wet conditions on the windward side give way to drier habitats on the leeward side. Annual rainfall runs from 1,500 to 2,000 millimeters, followed by a dry season of 4 to 5 months. The mean annual temperature sits between 24 and 27°C, though inland maximums can climb past 40°C.

We are writing to share some information about how hearing develops early in life. Most people learn spoken language in their first few years. When hearing is impaired, a child may lose the ability to speak, and may also struggle to understand what others are saying.

A severe hearing deficit often goes unnoticed at first. By the time parents realize their child is deaf, communication failures may already have strained family relationships and slowed the development of social skills. A child who grows up in a Deaf community and learns sign language rather than spoken language is largely spared these difficulties (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

Many developed countries evaluate a baby's hearing during the newborn period, so that a deaf child is not accidentally isolated within a hearing family. Sign language is a complete means of communication, but literacy still depends on understanding speech, since in most written languages the sound of a word is represented by symbols.

Someone who heard well enough to learn speech and reading keeps that ability even if hearing later deteriorates to the point of no longer hearing voices. Someone who never heard well enough to learn to speak rarely reads with proficiency (see [4]). Most evidence points to early identification of hearing impairment as the deciding factor in whether a child with very insensitive hearing learns spoken language well. Listening matters for second language learning too.

We hope this helps you understand why early intervention matters. If you have questions, please get in touch.

Warm regards,

Transduction is the conversion of physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. In the nervous system, it is the basic process by which stimuli become electrical signals. In sensory transduction, physical or chemical inputs are transformed by specialized sensory receptors into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system shows how this works. Within the retina, rod and cone cells form the bridge between the physical environment and neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it triggers a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. That molecular shift sets off a cascade of events that alters the photoreceptor's electrochemical gradient. As the gradient decreases, so do the electrical signals sent to the brain. More light hitting the photoreceptor therefore means fewer electrical impulses, and it is through this arrangement that the brain decodes the visual world.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

Mobile internet is expanding the immersive potential of storytelling through electronic games that run on portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest stage in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that try to make the player a co-author alongside the original designers, rather than just an avatar in a gameworld.

Location-aware interfaces let players fold places in the physical world into their gameworld, and the reverse, which is a first for interactive media. Beyond giving players a role in worldmaking, mobile games avoid linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling built on the player's experience of place.

The idea of "author-player" worldmaking has existed before, and mobile games push the process past the constraints of traditional video games. By extending worldmaking beyond the screen and into the physical world, location-aware interfaces use the player's sensory experiences of real places as storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games and describe our experience trying to use that potential through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often simply called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It grew out of a number of former industrial cities, among them Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

About five million people live in the region, so it is considerably larger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. There are plenty of motorways, but hitchhiking can still be difficult, mostly because of the confusing network of minor roads. The main motorways through the region are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitchhike here, stay on these main motorways. The smaller roads are hard to work with because hardly any transit traffic uses them. Germany is generally a pleasant country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is the least pleasant part of it for this purpose. Hitching within the Ruhr is a bit like hitching in a big city such as Istanbul: the cities are technically independent, but to a traveler they feel like districts of one enormous city.

We hope this helps you plan your trip, and we wish you a safe journey.

Best regards,

Here are the main findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

We calculated the total volume of lung tissue using the formula: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity resulting from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was computed as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between the PEEP and ZEEP states. We defined alveolar derecruitment as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, which were characterized by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As described in reference [21], we classified the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) as diffuse, patchy, or lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.
